scenes.viewerPurpose: The useful distinction is between an argument’s structure and the truth of its premises.

scenes.title: The wet street
scenes.viewerPurpose: The book turns this familiar mistake into a question about valid inference.
addOrChange: If rain makes a street wet, a wet street alone does not establish rain.
Another cause could produce the same observation.

scenes.title: Choose the right language
scenes.viewerPurpose: A formal proof still depends on the assumptions and definitions it starts from.
addOrChange: Propositional logic treats statements as blocks; predicates expose individuals and relationships.
Quantifiers, possibility, and time let later chapters express different kinds of questions.
